headline: OpenAI's first human rights lead, Sarah Yager, says the military use of AI for targeting and autonomous weapons "keeps me up at night".
score_reason: Lowered from 5 because the remarks were made on 6 Oct, before the scan window, and Fortune reported them that day.
importance_line: Civilians in conflict zones and AI users are affected by how militaries use the technology, but this is one employee's stated worry and the article does not say what OpenAI will change.
summary: Fortune reports that Sarah Yager, who joined OpenAI in June as its first human rights and responsible deployment lead, said at the ScaleUp:AI conference in New York on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 that "everyone is very worried and rightly so" about what militaries will do with AI in targeting and autonomous weapons. OpenAI approached her after it signed a contract in late February to deploy advanced AI in classified Department of War systems.
notes: Pool source Yahoo (Benzinga rewrite of Fortune); credited to Fortune, the first reporter. Score lowered 1 for age.
